text:
maria: Quick thread following yesterday's RFC: we need to pick between prefix-based routing (sigils) and canonical metadata-driven scoping. Can we list hard constraints?
aj: Constraints: (1) minimal added latency for hot paths, (2) safe migration for legacy keys, (3) clear auditability (no implicit scopes), (4) no accidental privilege escalation via crafted keys.
devon: Operational constraint: router needs to route to tenant-specific pools for caching and billing. A pure-metadata hop on every request adds 2-4ms at the moment.
lina: We measured DB lookups ~= 3ms p99 with our current cache misses. If router can make a safe routing hint without trusting it, we can reduce the cold-path.
maria: Proposal A: 'hint' prefix allowed only for routing. Header: Authorization: ApiKey hint=proj:alpha token=opaque-xyz
- router extracts hint and sends to pool;
- runtime always validates token against authn service which returns canonical {principal, projects, roles}.
- audit logs must record canonical project id from authn.
kevin: That seems OK. Important: hint must be unsigned and ephemeral. We should rate-limit routing hints to avoid sharding DoS.
aj: Proposal B: embed short cryptographic binder in key so router can verify scope without DB. e.g., key format: <opaque><.><hmac(scope, salt)>
- pros: router verifies binder quickly (in-memory HMAC key), no DB hop;
- cons: requires global key for HMAC management, rotation complexity, and leaks scope semantics into key format.
devon: HMAC binder could be rotated with key versioning. But rolling the global signer is operationally heavy and can brick trillions of keys if not careful.
lina: Also, binder approach still binds credential <-> scope; can't support dynamic role updates without reissuing keys. That breaks many enterprise workflows.
maria: For S2S, we also have two flows: long-lived service credentials (for infra control plane) and short-lived tokens (for app plane). How do these map to RBAC v2 resource templates?
aj: RBAC v2 suggestion: policy statements are triples: {subject, resource_template, verbs} where resource_template supports wildcards and param binding.
Example: "resource_template": "projects/{project_id}/models/{model_id}", verbs: ["invoke"]
- We can allow token issuance endpoints to mint tokens constrained to a concrete param set (project X, model Y) for time-limited use.
kevin: Good for least privilege. For convenience we should have presets: "model-invoke" -> expands to resource_template + verbs. Small teams can grant presets, power users can author templates.
devon: How about inheritance? If user has project-level role, they implicitly get resource-level access unless explicitly denied. We need explicit deny to opt-out. Deny semantics are complicated in distributed caches.
aj: Recommend avoid negative grants for now; rely on narrow grants + deny via policy shadowing in central authz service. We can introduce local deny later with stronger proofs.
lina: Cache design: credential_id -> policy_snapshot_id + last_seen_ts. Router caches policy_snapshot_id -> routing_hint (project). Authz service stores snapshot blobs. On rotation/role-change we bump snapshot_id and emit changefeed. Router subscribes and invalidates. TTL fallback ensures forward progress.
maria: Migration for legacy keys: offer a compatibility proxy that maps legacy prefixes to canonical project_id in authn service. New keys are minted metadata-first. Deprecation window 9 months? ops can shorten if adoption is fast.
kevin: We need metrics: fraction of requests routed by hint vs validated project, auth DB QPS, cache miss rates, number of times hint routing diverged from authn canonical project (a safety metric).
sec-bot: Policy: log AR-12 fields: principal_id, project_id(s), credential_id, token_kind, action, decision. Ensure logs are immutable and sampled for high-throughput routes.
aj: Edge-case: multi-project credentials (service role spanning projects). Router hints can't represent multiple projects. For routing, pick primary_project claim in token. Authz uses full list. Must document clearly.
devon: Rolling outage plan: if authn service degraded, routers can continue using last-known snapshot for N seconds, then fall back to safe-mode where only non-sensitive verbs allowed, or route to degraded pool with reduced concurrency. Emit alerts on failing-open.
lina: Implement 'safe-mode' feature toggle in router -> returns 403 for high-privilege verbs when auth backend unavailable. Ops can toggle per-region.
maria: Action items:
- maria: draft compatibility proxy spec + deprecation timeline (9 months tentative)
- devon: design cache + changefeed contract, define TTLs and subscribe model
- aj: prototype RBAC v2 YAML proto and presets for common roles (model-invoke, project-admin, billing-reader)
- kevin: propose metrics/dashboard widgets to monitor hint-vs-canonical divergence and fail-open counts

maria: Let's reconvene next Tue. Thanks all :raised_hands:
